items.title: Too Handsome To Ignore, But Is H.I.M Built To Last? - BW Marketing World
items.raw_summary: Actor Ranveer Singh and entrepreneur Aman Gupta’s H.I.M (Handsome Indian Man) enters the men’s personal care category with an unapologetic name, a founder story rooted in an unusual compliment and a proposition centred on Indian men’s grooming needs.The brand takes its cue from a remark Singh says a basketball player at an NBA game in the US told him: “You’re too handsome for an Indian man.” The founders turn the remark into a larger brand idea celebrating Indian masculinity, appearance and confidence.The launch film, ‘Tested On Ranveer Singh’, takes viewers behind the making of H.I.M, blending humour, science and grooming while positioning Singh as a co-founder and product participant rather than merely a celebrity endorser.What WorkedTurning a comment into a brand ideaThe origin story is the campaign’s strongest creative hook. “Too handsome for an Indian man” remark could have been dismissed as a throwaway compliment, but the brand turns it into a statement about confidence and Indian identity.The name H.I.M. is memorable, bold and conversation-worthy. It gives the brand a cultural entry point instead of starting with a conventional product-benefit pitch, while opening up a broader conversation around Indian masculinity and grooming.What's in a name?The name H.I.M (Handsome Indian Man) is striking, bold and instantly memorable. It stands out in a category often dominated by conventional, functional brand names, giving the brand a distinct identity and an easy conversation starter.Ranveer Singh as co-founder, not just celebrityThe ‘Tested On Ranveer Singh’ campaign’s credibility lever is Singh’s positioning as a co-founder and product participant. According to the brand, he tested more than 100 formulations, insisted on testing shampoo in Indian hard water and wanted face cream tested in heat and humidity rather than just air-conditioned laboratories.Singh’s involvement, from product development to packaging and naming the proprietary molecule IN·XT™, reinforces the narrative of a celebrity invested in building the business. For a category crowded with endorsements, this gives the partnership a more substantive reason to exist.Humour and science give the brand personalityMen’s personal care advertising often relies on predictable codes of muscularity, attractiveness and confidence. H.I.M’s irreverent positioning offers an opportunity to play with these conventions. Its humour, rooted in familiar Indian grooming behaviours, makes the brand relatable rather than aspirational in a conventional sense.The science-led proposition also adds substance. With eight products across face, body and hair, formulated for Indian skin, climate and biology, H.I.M connects its IN·XT technology to conditions such as hard water, heat and humidity. This makes the innovation story more relevant to consumers’ everyday experiences.A launch designed for creator participationThe creator-first launch was a smart extension of the brand’s audience strategy. Bringing together creators from fashion, comedy, music and fitness, alongside product trial stations, shower-thoughts recordings and fit-check mirrors, turned the event into a content-generating experience rather than just a launch venue.What Could Have Been StrongerThe brand risks being overshadowed by its foundersRanveer Singh’s personality, the origin anecdote and the celebrity-founder narrative are likely to be the campaign’s strongest recall drivers. The challenge is whether consumers will remember H.I.M as a distinct brand or primarily as Ranveer Singh and Aman Gupta’s venture. Celebrity-led awareness does not automatically translate into consideration, trial or repeat purchase.The product proposition needs to compete with the entertainmentThe storytelling makes for an engaging launch, but personal care purchase decisions ultimately rest on efficacy, price, convenience and trust. The campaign needs to clearly establish what makes H.I.M different, what IN·XT delivers and why consumers should switch from products they already use.The positioning needs to go beyond handsomeThe name is provocative and memorable, but the brand will need to build a broader narrative around grooming, self-care, confidence and individuality. If H.I.M wants to speak to the evolved Indian man, its communication must extend beyond physical appearance and embrace diverse identities and grooming habits.The VerdictH.I.M is attempting to build a brand at the intersection of celebrity, culture, entrepreneurship and product science. Its launch makes the brand feel like a conversation rather than a conventional grooming campaign. The name is memorable, the origin story is intriguing, and Singh’s reported involvement adds credibility.But the real test begins after the launch buzz. Can H.I.M turn personality into preference, science into trust, and attention into repeat purchase?H.I.M has made an attention-grabbing entrance. Now it needs to turn attention into a brand consumers believe in, buy and return to.
